reason: Several emission paths order their rows by iterating a plain set of strings, so PYTHONHASHSEED randomisation reorders them run to run; this item sorts them at the point of emission. Which files that can move was measured, not guessed: every corpus was rebuilt with PYTHONHASHSEED=12345 and 999 (lotr2008 also with 777), each build put through wiki-golden's own _normalise(), and the pairs diffed. Exactly five things moved and nothing else. (1) docs/map/index.html and docs/index.html — layout_areas discovers connected components by iterating adj[u] (a set[str]) and picks each BFS root with max() over a set, so component membership order, then the pos dict's insertion order, then the per-node RNG jitter draw all shift; every coordinate in the SVG changes. homers_lotr's docs/index.html is an author-supplied override with no map, so it moves in lotr2008/lotr2009 only, and an allowlist entry that does not move in a given corpus is fine. (2) docs/factions.html — three sorted() calls take a set of area/race ids under a display-name key, and equal names ("Great East Road" x3, "Old Forest", "The Misty Mountains") tie-break on set order; the fix adds the resref/race-id as the tie-break. (3) docs/conversations/*.html — dialog_teleports rows are appended while iterating script_teleport_tags (set[str]), which reorders the "Teleport destinations" table (observed on ctf_in_conv and koh_in_conv); the item-script caller set {resref, tag} in _index_item_script_callers feeds the same pages' "Triggered by" list. (4) docs/quests/*.html — _quest_start_locations iterates the grant script set and the dialog set, and the "Begins" cells are truncated to three, so hash order changes the cell CONTENT, not just its order (observed on quests/index.html); the same file's _items_html sorts a set of item resrefs under a display-name key, so a quest detail page could move too where two items in one cell share a name, hence the *.html glob rather than index.html alone. No line_patterns: reordered table rows and recomputed SVG coordinates cannot be characterised by a regex that is not vacuous, so the path allowlist is the whole prediction. Also fixed, and predicted to be output-NEUTRAL, so no path is declared for them: _annotate_dup_dest_tags iterating _referenced_tags (its only consumers sort the keys or read the value lists), and the {resref, tag} set on item pages (only two item pages in all three corpora carry a "Triggers conversation" section and each lists exactly one entry). Any other string-set iteration that reached emission would have moved a file under randomised hashing across three corpora and up to three seeds; none did, so nothing outside this list may change.
